text.p: A high-ranking delegation from Pakistan visited Kabul on Tuesday, the first ministerial visit to Taleban-held Afghanistan since the Islamic movement took over the capital on September 27.
No countries have yet recognised the Taleban government.
Acting information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told a news conference the delegation included Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar.

"There was a delegation which included high-ranking Pakistan officials, which came today, met with our authorities and they discussed some issues which normally two neighbouring countries should discuss, and returned to their country," he said.
The Taleban were formed in refugee camps in Pakistan two years ago and according to its opponents have enjoyed logistical support from Islamabad. Pakistan has denied such reports.

Mutaqi said the delegation also planned to visit Mazar-i-Sharif in northern territory held by General Abdul Rashid Dostum, who signed a political agreement with other militia opposing the Taleban on Monday.

"They had a chat here, and they told us they had a plan to go to Mazar-i-Sharif. We told them we don't have any problems with the forces in Mazar-i-Sharif and we are ready to solve the issues through negotiations and understanding with Mazar," Mutaqi said.
Pakistan has offered to negotiate between the Taleban and Dostum, who controls six northern provinces.
